messages:
priya: opened a PR to update the model catalog card for nebula-embed-2.1. main changes: clarify batching vs hard limits, add embedding throughput bench numbers, and include Python + Go SDK snippets for setting batching params. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1012 :wave:

priya: the goal is to avoid confusion where customers assume the "max_batch_size" in the catalog is a guaranteed cap for Dedicated pools. i'm proposing two columns: `recommended_batch_size` and `enforced_soft_limit` with notes per deployment mode.

tom: skimmed. we need explicit bench numbers in the card (items/sec) and a short note about median vs p95 latency. can you paste the perf-team run numbers?

priya: added a small bench table from perf-run-2026-03-01: 8xA10 (hosted): 12,300 items/s (1536-d); p95 latency 42ms. 1xT4 (edge-dedicated): 2,100 items/s; p95 110ms. included a short sentence: "actual throughput varies with dim, batching, and network overhead."

renee: please also add a compatibility note for "sharded-embeddings" variants. customers frequently hit NaNs if they assume sharding is transparent. propose row: "sharded-embeddings: supported (hosted), experimental (dedicated-edge)" and a note about recommended batch sizes (hosted: 256-1024, dedicated-edge: 64-256).

zack: wording nit: dedicated customers can often exceed hosted throughput if they reserve larger pools; saying "experimental" for dedicated-edge might read as limitation. suggest: "supported with caveats: see Dedicated migration guide" and link to the guide.

noah: (support) i can confirm the hosted numbers. for Dedicated we shouldn't promise >512 as a guaranteed limit on smaller GPUs (T4). better to say "recommended" ranges and link to the migration doc for tuning reserved pools. i'll file a ticket for dedicated tuning notes.

priya: agreed. updated the card to use "recommended_batch_size" and "notes" instead of hard promises. added a short Dedicated migration note: "Reserved pools may need autoscale configs and batch tuning; see /docs/migrate/dedicated-embeddings.md".

priya: added SDK snippets. Python async example:

```python
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def batch_embed(texts):
    async with AsyncClient() as c:
        resp = await c.embeddings.create(
            model="nebula-embed-2.1",
            input=texts,
            batch_config={"max_batch_size": 512, "flush_interval_ms": 25}
        )
        return resp.data
```

priya: and a minimal Go example (sync):

```go
client := redwood.NewClient(nil)
resp, err := client.Embeddings.Create(ctx, redwood.EmbeddingsCreateParams{
    Model: "nebula-embed-2.1",
    Input: []string{"a","b","c"},
    BatchConfig: map[string]interface{}{"max_batch_size": 512, "flush_interval_ms": 25},
})
if err != nil {
    log.Fatal(err)
}
fmt.Println(len(resp.Data))
```

priya: note in the PR that customers using sharded variants may need smaller `max_batch_size` to avoid out-of-memory.

tom: nice. small request: add an async python variant using `await` in the example call (you already do) and add link to the SDK batching docs.

priya: added the async note and link to /docs/sdk/batching.md. also updated the compatibility table anchor that previously pointed to a broken anchor.

docs-bot: link-check passed (commit abc123)  0 broken links.

renee: please add perf dashboard link in the card: https://perf.redwood.ai/embeds/nebula-2.1 so customers can see more runs.

priya: added the perf link and a short sentence: "See live runs on our perf dashboard for dimension-specific throughput."

noah: support confirms hosted wording is accurate. opening ticket #546 for Dedicated tuning notes (assign to infra).

priya: pushed final edits (commit f4d2be). i'll merge after infra ticket is created. anyone object?

tom: no objections from me. :thumbsup:

priya: merged and closed PR. closing thread. thanks folks!
